<reason>A more convincingly distinguished rooftop solar’s benefits from trading’s additional benefits. B offered plausible investment incentives and price discovery, but A supplied a regulated-tariff alternative and challenged B’s asymmetric expectations of regulation. A also answered both pressure questions directly. B’s crucial claim that buyers and sellers could both gain after full cost recovery remained inadequately supported, while its closing repeated the disputed curtailment story rather than resolving that accounting.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B answered the funding question with recovered waste, avoided distant generation, and retailer margins. A sharply countered that existing rooftop exports already avoid distant generation, contracts do not remove network constraints, and any avoidable markup must be weighed against platform costs and continuing service obligations. This substantially weakened B’s promised double benefit.</best_rebuttal>
